reason: B is the better proposal because its 100 h controlled oxidation test measures mass gain, spallation, scale chemistry, and retained mechanical properties against the untreated equiatomic alloy, extending beyond prior short exposures more clearly than A. Both are mechanistically questionable because 2–5 at.% Al may be insufficient for selective external Al2O3 formation in an Hf–Zr–Ti-rich alloy, but B’s higher Al level and longer, better-defined test make the claim more plausible and decisively testable.
